quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Business intelligence analysts produce financial and market intelligence by querying data repositories and generating periodic reports, and devise methods for finding patterns and trends in the available information.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Business Intelligence Analysts) include Business Intelligence Analyst (BI Analyst), Business Analyst, Competitive Intelligence Analyst and Market Intelligence Analyst.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What a business intelligence analyst does
paragraphs: Business intelligence analysts produce financial and market intelligence by querying data repositories and generating periodic reports, and devise methods for finding patterns and trends in the available information.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Business Intelligence Analysts. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Produce standard or custom reports that summarise business, financial or economic data.
Maintain and update business intelligence tools, databases and dashboards.
Identify and analyse industry or geographic trends that matter for business strategy.
Write the specifications for reports, dashboards and other outputs.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Common routes into this job on the Career Tree map: BCA (Bachelor of Computer Applications); B.Sc (Bachelor of Science); MBA (Master of Business Administration).
Less common routes on the map: BBA (Bachelor of Business Administration); B.Com (Bachelor of Commerce); B.Tech in Computer Science and Engineering.
